edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Εἰ οὖν οἱ ἐν παλαιοῖς πράγμασιν ἀναστραφέντες εἰς καινότητα ἐλπίδος ἦλθον, μηκέτι σαββατίζοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ κυριακὴν ζῶντες, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν ἀνέτειλεν δἰ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ὅν τινες ἀρνοῦνται, δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὑπομένομεν, ἵνα εὑρεθῶμεν μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου ἡμῶν: [2] πῶς ἡμεῖς δυνησόμεθα ζῆσαι χωρὶς αὐτοῦ, οὗ καὶ οἱ προφῆται μαθηταὶ ὄντες τῷ πνεύματι ὡς διδάσκαλον αὐτὸν προσεδόκων; καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, ὃν δικαίως ἀνέμενον, παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
pass_a_gloss: Supposing therefore that the people who conducted themselves in ancient practices arrived at a newness of hope, having ceased to sabbatize and instead living by the Lord's [day], on which our life likewise sprang up by means of him and his death (a death certain people refuse to admit), by which mystery we obtained believing, and on account of this we hold out, in order to be found Jesus Christ's disciples, he being our sole instructor: in what way will we manage to live without him, of whom the prophets also, being disciples by the Spirit, were expecting him as instructor? On account of this, the one they justly awaited, being present, roused them out of the dead.

lemmas.gloss: belonging to the Lord; the Lord's day

pass_b_english: If, then, those who had lived under the old order of things came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day, the day on which our life also dawned through him and through his death (which some deny, through that mystery we received faith, and for this reason we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only Teacher), how shall we be able to live apart from him?
Even the prophets were his disciples in the Spirit, and they looked for him as their Teacher. And for this reason the One they rightly awaited, when he came, raised them from the dead.

choices.english: they live by the Lord's day
choices.why: Adjective with ἡμέραν understood, set against σαββατίζοντες.
rejected: living in the observance of the Lord's Day

choices.why: Sunrise verb fits the day-image; life rose on the Lord's day.
ὅν agrees with θανάτου; the docetists denied the real death.
Capitalized as a title of Christ.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'whom some deny' leaves the antecedent open; the Greek ὅν most naturally takes θανάτου (his death). ANF 'Master' for διδάσκαλος; we use Teacher.

notes: 'Raised them from the dead' may allude to Matthew 27:52 (saints raised at the crucifixion); ANF tags it, but the wording is not shared, so it is not cited inline.
Some witnesses read κυριακὴν ζωήν ('the Lord's life'); Lake's text as supplied has κυριακήν alone. Check the apparatus before locking.
Source shows 'δἰ' for δι’; reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] is Magnesians 9 (Lake text), not another work. Greek «εἰς καινότητα ἐλπίδος ἦλθον, μηκέτι σαββατίζοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ κυριακὴν ζῶντες» matches A «arrived at a newness of hope, having ceased to sabbatize and instead living by the Lord's [day]» and B «came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day» (B compresses καινότητα, without reversing it). «ὅν τινες ἀρνοῦνται» stays on the death: A «a death certain people refuse to admit», B «which some deny». «δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὑπομένομεν, ἵνα εὑρεθῶμεν μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου ἡμῶν» matches A «by which mystery we obtained believing, and on account of this we hold out, in order to be found Jesus Christ's disciples, he being our sole instructor» and B «through that mystery we received faith, and for this reason we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only Teacher». The question «πῶς ἡμεῖς δυνησόμεθα ζῆσαι χωρὶς αὐτοῦ, οὗ καὶ οἱ προφῆται…προσεδόκων» is kept in A and, split but not contradicted, in B «how shall we be able to live apart from him» / «Even the prophets were his disciples in the Spirit, and they looked for him as their Teacher». «παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν» is A «being present, roused them out of the dead» and B «when he came, raised them from the dead» (presence/arrival of πάρειμι, same agent). No inline citation is wrong; the note withholds an unshared allusion. Title names the Lord's-day thought. Variant κυριακήν and δἰ are disclosed.

The source is Ignatius Magnesians 9 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Pass A preserves all clauses: the shift from Sabbath to Lord's day (κατὰ κυριακὴν ζῶντες), life dawning through Christ's death (ἀνέτειλεν), denial of his death (ὅν τινες ἀρνοῦνται), faith from mystery (διὰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν), endurance (ὑπομένομεν), becoming disciples (μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ), Christ as sole teacher (τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου), rhetorical question on living without him (πῶς ἡμεῖς δυνησόμεθα ζῆσαι χωρὶς αὐτοῦ), prophets as disciples expecting him (οἱ προφῆται μαθηταὶ ὄντες τῷ πνεύματι ὡς διδάσκαλον αὐτὸν προσεδόκων), and the One awaited raising them (ὃν δικαίως ἀνέμενον, παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν). Pass B renders this faithfully in two sentences, capturing all meaning without addition or contradiction. No scripture citations appear in source or translation, so none are required. Title 'Living by the Lord's Day' names the thought. Notes disclose OCR (δἰ) and variant (κυριακὴν ζωήν). All checks pass.
